gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI AC180 has an ECO mode that switches its outlets off on its own, or that a heater cycled by a thermostat sits at 0 W for long stretches, which is the kind of low load these auto-off modes look for.
standout_why: Compared against animalstart.com (smart thermostats, cited), pets.co.uk (cited), animalstart.com (controllers and backup power, rank 11) and Jackery's Explorer 1000 V2 Basic Information FAQ (cited in the third chat). Neither animalstart page mentions ECO mode or auto-off. pets.co.uk only says to check 'automatic transfer behaviour'. Jackery's cited FAQ already says Energy Saving Mode can be turned off and that its UPS switches in 20 ms and is 'not a 0 ms' UPS. So the rivals cover part of it. The part that would make it new is each maker's own watt threshold, time limit and default setting, and I could not open those (see unsourced). petco.com returned 403, so I could not check it.
decides: This doesn't change which station to buy. Every candidate checked has a 20 ms class transfer and some auto-off, so the finding becomes a setup step on the pick rather than a reason to choose one over another. Before trusting a heater on a thermostat to the AC180 or Explorer 1000 v2, turn off the low-load auto-off (BLUETTI ECO mode, Jackery Energy Saving Mode). Both makers document that you can. Neither unit's UPS is a 0 ms UPS (Jackery's own wording), so a thermostat or controller that reboots on a 20 ms dropout needs testing on the unit.

findings.label: Low-load auto-off feature
findings.value: ECO mode that turns the outputs on and off by itself to save energy
findings.note: The page's wording is 'a new ECO mode that automatically turns on/off to conserve energy'. It gives no watt threshold, time limit or default setting.

findings.label: UPS switchover time
findings.note: Maker's wording: 'automatically switches over in just 20ms during a power outage'. The page showed no price or stock.

findings.label: UPS switchover time and limit
findings.value: 20 ms; Jackery says it is not a 0 ms UPS
findings.note: Quotes: 'automatically switches to battery power within 20 ms (0.02 seconds)' and 'This function is not a 0 ms (no interruption) switching UPS.' ChatGPT cited this page.

findings.label: Exclusion the maker states for UPS use
findings.value: Do not connect devices that require a true uninterruptible power supply (data servers, workstations)
findings.note: Jackery's examples are servers and workstations. The page says nothing about reptile thermostats or heaters.

findings.label: Energy Saving Mode and auto power-off settings
findings.value: Energy Saving Mode can be turned off; the app allows auto power-off to be set to 'Never'
findings.note: The page lists 'Energy Saving Mode can be turned off: Supported' and an example setting of 'Auto Power-Off: Never'. It gives no default, watt threshold or time limit.

findings.label: Standby power consumption
findings.note: As Jackery lists it. At 18 W, the unit's own standby draw is close to a 24 W heat mat's draw, so runtime figures that leave it out overstate hours.
